title: Remove exposed PostgreSQL credential from repository
description: GitGuardian detected a live PostgreSQL connection URI committed in local development-tool configuration by commit 1161e5a. Remove the tracked local-only config, add an ignore rule preventing recurrence, verify no live PostgreSQL URI remains in tracked HEAD, then rotate the exposed database credential and update every authorized runtime consumer before resolving the incident.
acceptance_criteria: The local development configuration is untracked and ignored; tracked HEAD passes secret scanning; the PostgreSQL credential is rotated; production and authorized local consumers use the replacement; GitGuardian records the exposed value as revoked.
notes: Credential rotation and repository remediation completed on 2026-07-13. The exposed database user was revoked, GitGuardian confirmed revocation, tracked local development-tool configuration was removed and ignored, Render and the ignored local local database-tool configuration use the replacement user, and the ignored local .env now uses the same rotated external database URL. Verification passed: .env is mode 600, the URL matches local database-tool configuration, PostgreSQL authentication succeeds as the replacement user, TypeScript and ESLint pass, production is healthy, and no credential-bearing temporary file remains.
close_reason: Updated the ignored local .env to use the rotated database credential and verified successful authentication.

title: Add PostgreSQL credential pre-commit scanning
description: Default Gitleaks rules did not detect the live PostgreSQL DSN that GitGuardian flagged. Add a repository security check that rejects committed PostgreSQL connection strings containing non-placeholder credentials while allowing documented local-only examples and ignored environment files.
acceptance_criteria: A red-green automated fixture proves a production-shaped PostgreSQL DSN is rejected before commit; documented placeholder DSNs remain allowed; the check runs through the repository's normal verification or pre-commit workflow.
notes: Phase 3 scanner tests must cover Prisma destination-routing query overrides so credential-bearing URLs with loopback authorities and nonlocal query hosts cannot bypass detection.

title: Present and validate credential-free architecture
description: Present architecture, components, data flow, failure handling, and testing in reviewable sections.
acceptance_criteria: The user approves each design section before documentation begins.
notes: All design sections approved: hybrid Docker PostgreSQL plus host Next.js; loopback-only local database; local-only .env and database tools configuration; guarded destructive commands; reference-only seed; render psql diagnostics; staged PostgreSQL credential blocking; fail-closed errors; real Docker integration and full quality verification. Render allowlisting is gated until a trusted CIDR is supplied.
close_reason: User approved architecture, components, data flow, failure handling, and verification design sections.

title: Compare credential-free development approaches
description: Evaluate at least three viable approaches with security, operational, and developer-experience tradeoffs.
acceptance_criteria: A recommended approach is selected with rejected alternatives and concrete reasons.
notes: Compared three approaches: hybrid Docker PostgreSQL with host Next.js, fully containerized development, and host-installed PostgreSQL. Approved recommendation: hybrid Docker database plus host application because it reuses existing infrastructure, removes production credentials from local workflows, preserves fast Next.js iteration, and provides reliable disposable database lifecycle.
close_reason: User approved the hybrid Docker PostgreSQL plus host Next.js approach.

title: Clarify local database and secret-provider requirements
description: Resolve the intended local PostgreSQL workflow, production-access boundaries, and secret injection provider.
acceptance_criteria: The design has explicit choices for local database lifecycle, sanitized data, secret provider, and authorized remote access.
notes: Decisions: no 1Password or Doppler; normal development uses disposable local PostgreSQL; production diagnostics use authenticated render psql; local application and database tools workflows never retain or inject the Render production URL; local seeding is reference-only using the existing domains, themes, and badges, with development records created through the UI.
close_reason: Resolved the local database lifecycle, production access boundary, secret-provider choice, and reference-only seed policy.

title: Explore credential-free development context
description: Inspect the existing Docker, Prisma, environment, database tools, scripts, tests, documentation, and recent security changes before proposing architecture.
acceptance_criteria: Relevant project patterns, constraints, and gaps are summarized without exposing secrets.
notes: Context findings: docker-compose.yml already provides a real disposable PostgreSQL 15 database and uses local-only default credentials; Docker 29.6.1 and Compose 5.3.0 are available. The current ignored .env and local database-tool configuration contain the rotated Render URL. The seed writes only reference domains, themes, and badges, not production user data. README references a missing .env.example and obsolete docker-compose commands; Compose also warns that its version field is obsolete. Render CLI supports authenticated psql sessions. No automated test framework exists. Neither 1Password CLI nor Doppler CLI is installed.
close_reason: Inspected the existing local database, secret files, tooling, documentation, seed behavior, tests, and recent changes without exposing credentials.
